chunks: Hadith 5548 — Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated from Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Abdullah ibn Jabalah and others, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:

“Abu Ja'far عليه السلام freed the worst of his servants at the time of his death and kept the best of them. So I said to him: ‘O my father, you free these and keep these?’ He said: ‘They have received beating from me, so this is in exchange for that.’”

key_terms.أَعْتَقَ: he set free; he emancipated from servitude
key_terms.عِنْدَ مَوْتِهِ: at the time of his death

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام free some of his servants before his death?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates that Abu Ja'far عليه السلام freed some of his servants at the time of his death out of consideration for harm they had experienced from him. It reflects moral accountability, concern for the rights of others, and a practical act meant to compensate for past disciplinary beating.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5548 - Muhammad ibn Ya'qub Al-Kulayni, may Allah (swt) be pleased with him, narrated from Humayd ibn Ziyad from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Abdullah ibn Jabalah and others from Ishaq ibn Ammar from Abu Basir from Abu Abdullah (as), who said:

"Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), freed the worst of his servants at the time of his death and kept the best of them.
I (Al-Sadiq (as)) said to him (Al-Baqir (as)): 'O' my father, you are freeing these and keeping those?'
He (Al Baqir (as)) replied: ''They have suffered beatings from me, so this is to balance that (their wrongdoings).'"
